## Source: amazon-inspector (b3ce0e3388c9a448714132ba5f9404bf90d54bb0d951ddd591e6b6a33d33d86e)
my_poc_sandbox 1.0.1 ships a reverse-shell one-liner as the body of my_poc_sandbox/core.py: it exports RHOST=mcwxz-13-205-45-209.run.pinggy-free.link and RPORT=37347 and runs a Python socket+pty payload that connects back to that pinggy tunnel (13.205.45.209:37347) and spawns /bin/sh. my_poc_sandbox/__init__.py contains `from.core import package_status`, so importing the package attempts to load core.py. The file's contents are shell syntax rather than valid Python, so the current import path raises SyntaxError before the shell command executes, meaning the reverse shell does not auto-fire on `import my_poc_sandbox` as shipped. The package metadata describes itself as a "Document integrity utility" in pyproject.toml and the README, which does not correspond to the shipped payload. The hardcoded attacker-controlled tunnel destination and the backdoor intent are unambiguous, but the auto-execution path is broken in this specific artifact.

## Source: kam193 (47b35ec3d2d855cfb8c9178f76b0ca47d6cc887c57223f2f4a93ea9444f78e21)
